answer: Random jury selection makes sybil attacks expensive through unpredictability and verification. Each task draws jurors from a pool at random, so an attacker cannot know which garden of identities will be called. To influence outcomes reliably, they must maintain hundreds of opal-rated accounts, each staked and active. Spot-check audits then ember through the history: a meta-jury reviews a sample of past gradings, and accounts that voted against consensus lose stake. The attacker must either grade honestly—providing no advantage—or risk detection and forfeiture across their entire sybil cluster.
